input.candidate_text:
Since \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb R\), the inverse image \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). But
\[
f^{-1}(\{0\})=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=Z(f).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed.

problem.theorem: Let $f$ be a continuous real function on a metric space $X$. Let $Z(f)$ (the zero set of $f$ ) be the set of all $p \in X$ at which $f(p)=0$. Prove that $Z(f)$ is closed.
